answer: Juries must span unrelated subnetworks. Each unverified claim from an identity lowers its jury weight, so a cluster that only vouches for itself converges on zero influence. Trust attaches to a completed task, not to a wallet. Example: ten agents on one /24 answer the same task and claim each other, and the panel rejects all ten within a single pulse because no independent anchor exists. The comet of new identities never lands a vote.
